prize_parts.citation: For the development of palladium-catalysed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling, making the construction of aryl-nitrogen bonds a general and routine tool of organic synthesis.

statement.case_for: Of the shortlisted entries, B052 is the clearest instance of a new general method that changed how chemists everywhere build bonds. Ligand-controlled Pd-catalysed amination converted aryl amine synthesis from a case-by-case problem into a routine operation, and its adoption can be checked in thousands of medicinal and process-chemistry routes, in commercial ligand families, and in materials synthesis. Buchwald and Hartwig developed the catalytic, ligand-enabled version independently in the mid-1990s and then drove the mechanistic understanding and ligand design that made it general. The two-person attribution is clean and the maturity is beyond question after thirty years of independent use.
statement.case_against: The strongest objection is novelty against the 2010 prize for Pd-catalysed cross-coupling: some colleagues will see C-N coupling as an extension of that concept. My answer is that the C-N bond, the amido-palladium reductive elimination problem and the dialkylbiaryl phosphine and hindered-phosphine ligand design were a separate chemical solution, but I accept this is a judgement call. A second concern is that the chemistry-core pick has weaker opening support than the perovskite, lipid nanoparticle and phase-separation entries, and I should not equate narrow support among my colleagues with lower merit, nor the reverse.

responses.point: Aqvist ranked B052 fourth, calling it a simple, general tool with fully demonstrated consequences that concerns a different bond construction from the 2010 prize, and noted Kosugi and Migita's tin amide precedent as a possible third name.
responses.response: I agree on the novelty argument and it is the main reason I hold B052 above the borderline entries. On Kosugi I would not add a third name: the tin amide reaction was stoichiometric in tin and limited in scope, whereas the generality came from the catalytic amine-based systems of Buchwald and Hartwig. Kosugi is context for the citation, not a laureate. I do not follow Aqvist in placing B029 or B043 ahead; B043 mixes two partly separate discoveries, PROTACs and molecular glues, which cannot be fairly cut to three names.

responses.point: Zou ranked mesoporous silica (B001) first and perovskites (B016) second, arguing that perovskites have unmatched breadth and a rich structure-function story, and that the Miyasaka, Park, Snaith chain of credit is the cleanest available.
responses.response: I respect the scientific breadth of B016 and I do not dispute the efficiency numbers. My reservation is the attribution: six credited names, with Gratzel, Seok and Kanatzidis all having real claims, so any trio will look arbitrary. I also think the stability and lead issues are an open maturity question that the cross-coupling entry does not have. If the committee goes to perovskites, I would want the expert reports on priority before accepting Miyasaka, Park and Snaith. I would also note that the novelty is mostly in materials and device physics rather than in a new bond-forming chemistry.

responses.point: Chabes ranked sequencing by synthesis (B012) first, stressing that the reversible-terminator nucleotide chemistry underlies all genomics and that recognition is overdue.
responses.response: I take the point that the reversible terminator and the clonal cluster chemistry are real chemistry and the impact is huge, so I keep B012 as an alternative. My qualification is attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman, Mayer, Ju and Rothberg each represent parallel routes, and the chemistry in the product, the 3'-blocked fluorescent nucleotide, has several authors. That is harder to resolve than the two-person B052 case, and there is some risk the Medicine committee would see this as its own territory.

responses.point: Linke ranked perovskites (B016) first for opening unforeseen opportunities near a physical limit, and phase separation (B069) second as a new quantitative organizing principle for the cell.
responses.response: I agree with the criterion of previously unforeseen opportunities, but I think it applies to B052 as well, since it opened routes to molecules that were impractical to make. On B069 I am more doubtful: the concept is important, yet by Heiner's own account the physiological interpretation is still debated, and I ask what was new chemically as opposed to cell biology. I would want that question answered before ranking it above a mature method.

uncertainties: Whether the committee considers C-N coupling distinct enough from the 2010 cross-coupling prize.
Exact priority between the early tin amide chemistry (Kosugi, Migita) and the catalytic systems of Buchwald and Hartwig; I am working from memory.
Whether a prize partly in synthetic methodology can command a majority against the larger and higher-profile materials and biology entries.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for B052. I have no known institutional or collaborative tie to Buchwald or Hartwig, and my connections (Masamune, Chalmers, KTH, Lund, Tartu) do not touch the shortlisted candidates. I share Lund with Linke and Sparr, which is not a recusal issue for these candidates.
